[USER] The Truth in Lending Act applies to loans made to: A. Businesses B. Consumers C. Nonprofit organizations D. Government agencies  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Truth in Lending Act (TILA) applies to loans made to consumers. The correct answer is B: Consumers.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] TILA is a federal law that was enacted to protect consumers from deceptive lending practices by requiring lenders to disclose certain information about the terms and conditions of their loans.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] TILA applies to a wide range of consumer credit transactions, including mortgages, home equity loans, credit cards, and other types of consumer loans.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] TILA requires lenders to provide borrowers with clear and concise information about the terms and conditions of their loans, including the annual percentage rate (APR), the total finance charge, and the total amount financed.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] This information must be disclosed in writing and must be presented in a clear and conspicuous manner so that borrowers can make informed decisions about whether to take out a loan.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] TILA applies to loans made to individuals, but it does not apply to loans made to businesses, nonprofit organizations, or government agencies.  
[USER] Which is a closed-end loan? A. Adjustable-rate mortgage B. Home equity line of credit C. Credit card D. Debit card  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A closed-end loan is a type of loan that involves a single lump-sum borrowing, with a fixed repayment schedule and a fixed interest rate.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Examples of closed-end loans include mortgages, car loans, and personal loans.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The correct answer is A: Adjustable-rate mortgage.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] An adjustable-rate mortgage (ARM) is a type of closed-end loan that allows the lender to adjust the interest rate on the loan periodically based on market conditions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The borrower is required to repay the loan in fixed installments over the life of the loan.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Other examples of closed-end loans include fixed-rate mortgages, car loans, and personal loans.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Open-end loans are loans that allow the borrower to borrow and repay funds repeatedly up to a certain credit limit.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Examples of open-end loans include credit card accounts and home equity lines of credit (HELOCs).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Credit cards and HELOCs are not closed-end loans, as the borrower is able to borrow and repay funds repeatedly within a certain credit limit
